Note::count_substring¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::count_substring(std::string_view needle) const

Count Occurrences Of A Literal Substring In Each Cell¶

count_substring(needle) returns, for each cell, how many times the literal string needle occurs in it. It is the counting member of the substring family — contains answers “any?”, this answers “how many?” Use it to weight rows, spot the cell with the most separators, or turn a Note into a numeric feature.

Occurrences are counted left to right and non-overlapping: after a match the scan resumes at its end, so "aaaa" contains "aa" twice, not three times. The match is literal — no regex, no case folding.

Return value¶

An Int64 Note with the receiver’s shape, one native count per cell. Use integers() for a borrowed contiguous host view.

Edge cases¶

  • An empty needle yields 0 for every cell (it is not counted between every character).

  • A needle that never appears yields 0.

Example 1: A Basic Count¶

const auto counts =
    pluss::make_note({"banana", "aaaa", "xyz", ""}).count_substring("a");
std::cout << "[";
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < counts.integers().size(); ++i)
  std::cout << (i ? ", " : "") << counts.integers()[i];
std::cout << "]\n";

Output¶

[3, 4, 0, 0]

Example 2: Matches Do Not Overlap¶

const auto counts = pluss::make_note({"aaaa"}).count_substring("aa");
std::cout << "[" << counts.integers()[0] << "]\n";

Output¶

[2]

Example 3: An Empty Needle Counts Zero¶

const auto counts = pluss::make_note({"abc"}).count_substring("");
std::cout << "[" << counts.integers()[0] << "]\n";

Output¶

[0]

Example 4: A Multi-Character Needle¶

const auto counts =
    pluss::make_note({"a-b-c-d", "no dashes"}).count_substring("-");
std::cout << "[";
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < counts.integers().size(); ++i)
  std::cout << (i ? ", " : "") << counts.integers()[i];
std::cout << "]\n";

Output¶

[3, 0]

See Also¶

  • Note::contains: the yes/no version.

  • NoteRegexAccessor::count: count matches of a pattern rather than a literal.

  • NoteRegexAccessor::findall: return the matches, not just their count.
